## This week in brief

- **Co-packaged optics moved from component demos to system-level proof.** Wiwynn, Ayar Labs and GUC ran a live CPO rack at OCP Summit using UCIe die-to-die links, with company-reported ~30 W per 1.6T pluggable port versus ~9 W for the CPO path ([Co-Packaged Optics Clears System-Level Proof](https://www.techtimes.com/articles/329193/20261019/co-packaged-optics-clears-system-level-proof-wiwynn-runs-live-ai-rack-ocp-summit.htm)). Celestica announced a 102.4 Tbit/s CPO switch with full liquid cooling, but no independent measurements were published ([Celestica DS6005](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMisAFBVV95cUxOMUltT0VyeHRMUTEtcENGUkloRk5VUllHLUl0TUZJLWMyVnZyOTc2VDNPN05WbzdFdXJTOTRXX1d4NTJwS0s4Q0M1emtGNzd5c3VxRlhVU25ibU1MUWhja3YyLVNGV1h4NEdKWktOazlfdHJtUzVaQjlDWEVtT19RaWE0aWZaTHYtNjR4UFJjelAweTNHa0lIcUJ3MUdmdE9UMTVvMDlBRFVQb0d6bzJtUQ?oc=5)).
- **448G/lane electrical interfaces remain unresolved.** OIF reporting indicates 448G-PAM4 needs roughly 106–112 GHz Nyquist, and connector bandwidth may decide PAM4 versus PAM6, which carries about a 3.6 dB SNR penalty ([Defining Electrical 448G/Lane](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMikgFBVV95cUxQNnM0NFhJQ1d0UDNBZ2xCUzllQ05adm1WV0ZXQ0ZzazZTemlMODVFTmdUUHdzUnNKekcxRWxHcGVQWWM4a0xYWksyRVNSMmNtLUgzclpDeXMzUVlWc2RBOVA2Szc5TXdEMDVrYkdzODZ4d3lvb3I5Z2FwR05NMFFGaEgyNHVSQ0U0NFRJNEdjalNlQQ?oc=5)).
- **Busbar heating under harmonic current was quantified experimentally.** A 40×10 mm copper busbar at ~400 A showed analytical prediction errors of −3.1% to +0.4% for mixed spectra, but underestimation of 3.4–8.8% at 100–250 Hz ([Harmonics and Busbar Heating](https://doi.org/10.3390/en19204940)).
- **A data-driven Zn-Ni plating model linked lab and plant data.** Reported R² values included 88% for coating thickness and 92% classifier accuracy in the test environment; plant-only process models reached 92–94% ([Data-Driven Modelling of an Electroplating Process](https://finishingandcoating.com/index.php/plating/3058-from-lab-to-plant-data-driven-modelling-of-an-electroplating-process)).
- **LPBF thin-wall transferability failed for the smallest gyroid.** G100 showed Dice 0.479–0.564 with missing material but no XRD crystallinity; G200/G300 improved geometry but showed crystallinity ([Zr-based BMG gyroids](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00170-026-19359-w)).

## Themes to watch

Optical interconnect is converging on co-packaged and near-packaged architectures, with serviceability (external lasers, detachable fiber arrays) framed as a qualification requirement. Electrical signaling at 448G/lane is gated by connector and channel bandwidth. In power interconnects, joint resistance and harmonic content, not bar cross-section alone, dominate local heating. Plating and surface-finish sources remain largely vendor guidance; the Zn-Ni study is the notable data-backed exception.

## Evidence gaps

Most plating, busbar and thermal items are vendor-authored with no measured results. CPO power and bandwidth figures are company-reported. The TiC-reinforced 7075 laser-welding paper had no retrievable abstract or body text, so no findings can be stated. Several papers are accepted manuscripts or abstracts only, limiting verification.

## This week in brief

- **Co-packaged optics (CPO) moved toward platform integration.** Celestica announced the DS6005, a 102.4Tbps, 64×1.6TbE liquid-cooled ORv3 switch built on Broadcom's Tomahawk 6 Davisson, with optical engines on the ASIC package and field-replaceable external lasers ([Celestica Introduces the DS6005 Data Center Switch with Co-Packaged Optics to Enable Power-Efficient AI Fabrics - GlobeNewswire](https://news.google.?oc=5)). Wiwynn, Ayar Labs and GUC showed a live ORv3 compute system with TeraPHY optical engines and telemetry, but supplied no quantitative figures ([Wiwynn, Ayar Labs, and GUC Advance Co-Packaged Optics with Live Demonstration of Integrated Optical Compute System at OCP Global Summit 2026 - PR Newswire](https://news.google.?oc=5)).
- **Busbar thermal risk got a simulation-based surrogate.** A Frontiers paper trained XGBoost on 3D electro-thermal FE cases for bolted switchgear joints, reporting R²=0.990±0.005 and RMSE=1.877±0.542 K, with load current and contact resistance dominant in SHAP; the authors state it is geometry-specific and not experimentally validated ([Interpretable surrogate modeling for load-aware thermal risk assessment of bolted switchgear busbar joints using electro-thermal simulation](https://doi.org/10.3389/fmech.2026.1904437)).
- **EV busbar joining and interconnect guidance stayed vendor-advisory.** Han's Laser described an integrated laser cleaning/welding gantry for copper busbars without measured weld or throughput data ([Integrated Laser Cleaning and Welding System for Automotive Busbars - Han's Laser](https://www.hanslaserus.com/knowledge/integrated-laser-cleaning-and-welding-system-for-automotive-busbars/)); NovaEuris set procurement criteria (T2/TU1 copper, nickel 3–8 µm, ≤65 K rise) as advisory only ([2026 Energy Storage PACK Busbar Selection Guide](https://www.novaeuris.com/buyer-guide/2026-energy-storage-pack-busbar-selection-guide-co.html)).
- **Additive manufacturing papers emphasized process control.** A review mapped GMAW/GTAW/PAW adaptation to WAAM, noting CMT's low heat input and spatter ([Application and Adaptation of Arc-Based Welding Processes to Wire Arc Additive Manufacturing: A Review](https://doi.org/10.3390/ma19204362)); a separate study reported a simulated intralayer L-PBF controller cutting threshold exceedances 99.98% in one layer, evaluated in MATLAB rather than on the printer ([Design of an intralayer data-based controller for laser powder bed fusion processing](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00170-026-19180-5)).

## Themes to watch

CPO is shifting from component demos to rack-level integration, but power and latency claims remain vendor statements. Contact-surface reliability (plating porosity, busbar joints) is being addressed through advisory guides and simulation rather than published test data. AM process control is maturing in simulation, with physical validation still pending.

## Evidence gaps

No independent measured CPO performance, no experimental validation of the busbar surrogate, and no quantitative data from the busbar welding or selection guides. Several CPO items were search snippets only. No patents were supplied, so no legal status or novelty can be assessed.

topic_weeks.synthesis_md:
## Key developments

**Papers — process–geometry coupling.** A PBF-LB study found that parameters optimized on dense Zr-based bulk metallic glass cubes did not transfer cleanly to thin-walled gyroids: 100 μm walls showed missing material (Dice 0.479–0.564) but no XRD-detectable crystallinity, while 200–300 μm walls improved geometric agreement (Dice up to 0.865) but showed wall thickening and crystallinity [Transferability of laser powder bed fusion parameters...](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00170-026-19359-w). A separate FEA study reports that feedforward laser power control stabilized simulated melt-pool transverse area in thermally unstable regions of IN625 multi-track scans, though quantitative results were not verifiable from the accessible text [Computational modeling of melt pool evolution...](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00170-026-19361-2).

**Papers — modeling and materials.** A coupled kMC–FE framework for binder-jetted 316L sintering reports nonlinear anisotropy evolution and is flagged as an accepted manuscript subject to edits [Continuum meso-macro multiscale modeling...](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1038/s44334-026-00118-4). A sodium silicate binder abstract reports 6.80 MPa flexural strength at 120 °C versus 1.42 MPa for a conventional binder [Development of a low-temperature curable...](https://doi.org/10.1108/rpj-04-2026-0227). A VPP coating study reports Ra reduced below 0.15 μm and transmittance raised to ~86–89%, with residual haze [Controlled resin coating...](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00170-026-19372-z).

**Papers — monitoring.** A CNN feasibility study reports ~84% validation accuracy using surrogate labels, not physically verified defects [A vision-based deep convolutional neural network...](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00170-026-19346-1); a review synthesizes 75 papers into a conceptual defect-detection framework without new experiments [Data driven framework...](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44245-026-00237-4).

**News.** JOME Engineering reportedly WAAM-printed a marine propeller from a scan, citing ~60% lead-time reduction [JOME Engineering...](https://3dprintingindustry.com/news/jome-engineering-3d-prints-marine-propeller-from-a-scan-cutting-lead-time-by-about-60-255801/).

## Evidence gaps

No patents appear in the supplied records. Several items are abstracts or partial texts, limiting verification. The news claim is single-source and unverified. No cross-record trend can be established from this small, heterogeneous sample.

## Key developments

- A Renault recall (campaign 0FDZ) of Captur and Symbioz hybrids, per the EU Safety Gate alert, cites a potentially compromised busbar-to-relay connection in the traction battery; resistance at the joint converts current to heat, which may cause abnormal heating and fire risk. No fires were reported in Europe, and the remedy procedure is not described [Renault Issues Fire Risk Recall](https://www.autoevolution.com/news/renault-issues-fire-risk-recall-for-captur-and-symbioz-hybrid-vehicles-277276.html).
- Practitioner guidance argues busbar cross-section alone does not set performance: terminal constriction, contact force, joint resistance and adjacent heat sources can dominate local heating, with worked examples (200 A at 40 mm² = 5 A/mm²; a 100 µΩ joint dissipates 4 W at 200 A versus 10 W at 250 µΩ) [HESS Copper Busbars](https://www.stamping-welding.com/info/hess-busbar-interconnect-design-103708714.html).
- Field rule-of-thumb current densities are given as ~8–10 A/mm² continuous for copper (15–20 A/mm² pulsed), with a ~30% margin and four-wire milliohm testing of series joints [Lithium Battery Pack Busbar Design](https://chinadronebattery.com/lithium-battery-pack-busbar-design-and-current-density-limits/).
- A buyer guide flags 300+ Ah cells pushing toward thicker, wider and laminated busbars, plus EU Batteries Regulation and CBAM documentation demands [NovaEuris guide](https://www.novaeuris.com/buyer-guide/how-to-choose-copper-busbars-for-2026-energy-stora.html).
- Monitoring guidance says busbars and terminals can be local heat sources, so sensing should extend beyond cells [ESHINE](https://www.eshine-cd.com/news/battery-temperature-monitoring-bess-sensing-system-protection.html).
- Tide Rock acquired Electro-Spec, a plating firm serving battery applications [Finishing and Coating](https://finishingandcoating.com/index.php/plating/3061-tide-rock-acquires-electro-spec-launches-specialty-surface-finishing-platform).

## Evidence gaps

All supplied records are news or vendor/practitioner articles; no patents or peer-reviewed papers are included. No measured test results or failure rates are reported, and no trend can be established from these sources alone.

## Key developments

Co-packaged optics (CPO) dominated the week, moving from component demos toward system-level and manufacturing framing. Wiwynn, Ayar Labs and GUC ran a live CPO AI rack at OCP Summit using UCIe die-to-die links and external lasers, with company-reported power of ~9 W versus ~30 W per 1.6T pluggable port [Tech Times](https://www.techtimes.com/articles/329193/20261019/co-packaged-optics-clears-system-level-proof-wiwynn-runs-live-ai-rack-ocp-summit.htm). Celestica announced the DS6005, a 102.4 Tbit/s CPO switch with full liquid cooling, though no independent measurements were published [igor´sLAB](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMisAFBVV95cUxOMUltT0VyeHRMUTEtcENGUkloRk5VUllHLUl0TUZJLWMyVnZyOTc2VDNPN05WbzdFdXJTOTRXX1d4NTJwS0s4Q0M1emtGNzd5c3VxRlhVU25ibU1MUWhja3YyLVNGV1h4NEdKWktOazlfdHJtUzVaQjlDWEVtT19RaWE0aWZaTHYtNjR4UFJjelAweTNHa0lIcUJ3MUdmdE9UMTVvMDlBRFVQb0d6bzJtUQ?oc=5).

Standards and supply-chain signals followed: the Advanced Photonics Coalition published five optical manufacturing specifications covering CPO, silicon photonics and multicore fibre [IN Electronics & Design](https://www.inelectronics.co.uk/photonics-coalition-publishes-five-optical-manufacturing-specifications/). Nvidia is reported to target 15x optical-engine capacity by 2027 via suppliers including SPIL [ET Telecom](https://telecom.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/devices/nvidia-targets-15x-more-optics-capacity-for-ai-data-centers-by-2027-report/135105414).

On electrical interfaces, OIF's 448G/lane work was presented at OCP, with connector bandwidth and PAM4/PAM6 trade-offs flagged as open questions [Simple Tech and Trend](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMikgFBVV95cUxQNnM0NFhJQ1d0UDNBZ2xCUzllQ05adm1WV0ZXQ0ZzazZTemlMODVFTmdUUHdzUnNKekcxRWxHcGVQWWM4a0xYWksyRVNSMmNtLUgzclpDeXMzUVlWc2RBOVA2Szc5TXdEMDVrYkdzODZ4d3lvb3I5Z2FwR05NMFFGaEgyNHVSQ0U0NFRJNEdjalNlQQ?oc=5).

## Evidence gaps

All performance and capacity figures are company- or press-reported, not peer-reviewed. No independent CPO-versus-pluggable measurements, customer qualification results, or deployment data were supplied. Market forecasts are vendor estimates. No trend can be established from the connector-plating explainers, which report no measured results.

## Key developments

- A practitioner article on lithium battery pack busbars gives rule-of-thumb continuous current densities (about 4 A/mm² for nickel-plated steel, ~6 A/mm² for pure nickel, ~5–6 A/mm² for aluminum, 8–10 A/mm² for copper) and recommends a ~30% margin and four-wire milliohm testing of every series joint; no measured data are provided [Lithium Battery Pack Busbar Design and Current Density Limits](https://chinadronebattery.com/lithium-battery-pack-busbar-design-and-current-density-limits/).
- A laser-equipment vendor application note addresses fiber-laser welding of 0.5–3 mm aluminum, attributing defects to high reflectivity (~90% at 1,080 nm), high thermal conductivity, the Al2O3 film, and solidification shrinkage/porosity, and supplies starting parameters and argon shielding guidance; the speed comparisons are vendor claims and customer testimonials, not independent measurements [How to Adjust Laser Welding Parameters for Thin Aluminum Sheets - LaserMen](https://lmlasercnc.com/article/how-to-adjust-laser-welding-parameters-for-thin-aluminum-sheets/).
- A commercial explainer compiles typical copper busbar properties (C11000 at about 101% IACS) and compares copper with 1350 aluminum (about 61–62% IACS, roughly 1.6× cross-section and about 0.5× weight for equal resistance); these are published typical figures, not verified measurements [Copper Busbar: The Numbers Behind Every Busbar](https://payapress.com/copper-busbar/).
- A paper is indexed on numerical analysis of molten pool-particle behavior in wire-fed laser welding of 7075 aluminum with TiC-reinforced filler wire, but only bibliographic metadata was available [Numerical analysis of molten pool-particle behavior in wire-fed laser welding of 7075 aluminum alloy with TiC reinforced filler wire](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.optlastec.2026.116742).
- A lubricant supplier article discusses forming lubricants for aluminum and AHSS, listing requirements such as substrate compatibility and chlorine-free formulations, without measured performance data [Metal Forming Lubricants | FUCHS OIL CORP. (CZ), SPOL. ...](https://www.fuchs.com/cz/en/company/actualities/technical-articles/metal-forming-lubricants/).

## Evidence gaps

No peer-reviewed results, measured joint performance, or commercial adoption data are supplied. The single paper record lacks retrievable content, so no findings can be stated. No trend in dissimilar aluminum joining can be established from these records.

## Key developments

- A paper reports COF/GO hybrid nanocomposites made by in situ polymerization as lubricant additives in PAO 10. The authors report that TADM/GO at 0.05 wt.% reduced friction coefficient by 30.43% and wear volume by 95.58% versus neat PAO 10 in reciprocating sliding, and by 35.71% and 69.37% under four-ball conditions at 392 N over 4 h [Covalent organic framework/graphene oxide hybrids via in situ polymerization as high-performance lubricant additives](https://doi.org/10.26599/frict.2026.9441328). These are author-reported results in an article listed as just accepted and under peer review, not a finalized peer-reviewed record [same source](https://doi.org/10.26599/frict.2026.9441328).

- A paper on Three Gorges ship lift gearboxes links high-temperature lubricant oxidation to formation of acidic polar molecules, rising acid number and kinematic viscosity, and declining tribological performance, combining experiments with ReaxFF simulations [Effect of lubricant oxidation on tribological performance of gear contact interfaces in three gorges ship lift: experiments and simulation](https://doi.org/10.1108/ilt-02-2026-0074). Only the abstract was available, so numerical results could not be verified [same source](https://doi.org/10.1108/ilt-02-2026-0074).

## Evidence gaps

No patents are present. No commercial adoption, legal status, or independently verified performance is evidenced. With two papers (one abstract-only, one not yet peer-reviewed) and two manufacturer pages, no trend can be established.

## Key developments

Test-data augmentation failed at process level due to unrecorded zinc dosing from immersed anodes [Data-Driven Modelling of an Electroplating Process](https://finishingandcoating.com/index.php/plating/3058-from-lab-to-plant-data-driven-modelling-of-an-electroplating-process).

## Key developments

**Papers (all four records are journal papers; no patents or news were supplied).**

- Aluminum MEX-AM: debinding route choice affected sintered density. Wick debinding in an Al2O3 powder bed gave more uniform microstructure and higher density than solvent-plus-thermal debinding, which caused slight surface oxidation; binder removal reached ≥96 wt.% in both routes, and extending sintering dwell from 2 h to 10 h raised relative density from ~97% to ~98% [Material extrusion-based additive manufacturing of aluminum feedstocks with a focus on the debinding process](https://doi.org/10.1007/s40964-026-01995-z).
- L-PBF control: a data-based predictive FIR proportional controller was tested only in closed-loop MATLAB simulation using photodiode data from a Ti-6Al-4V spinal cage build, reporting a 99.98% reduction in threshold-exceeding samples in the studied layer; physical-printer deployment was not demonstrated [Design of an intralayer data-based controller for laser powder bed fusion processing](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00170-026-19180-5).
- WAAM review: positions GMAW/GTAW/PAW as the metallurgical foundation of WAAM and notes CMT's low heat input and spatter, with process choice depending on alloy, deposition rate, geometry, and surface quality [Application and Adaptation of Arc-Based Welding Processes to Wire Arc Additive Manufacturing: A Review](https://doi.org/10.3390/ma19204362).

## Technical developments

Rosenberger announced GFC® (Glass Fiber Connector), a fiber-optic connector standard for in-vehicle data communication, positioned as a complement to existing coaxial and differential copper links as automotive bandwidth demand rises. The announcement states support for data rates above 50 Gbps over distances up to 40 meters and full IEEE 802.3cz compliance (https://rna.rosenberger.com/news-events/news/gfc-optical-connectivity-in-vehicles). It is described as developed for harsh automotive environments per ISO 24581, meeting mechanical and environmental requirements of ISO 8092 and DIN 70214, and having passed Arizona dust and water tests (same URL). The connector supports OM3 and OM4 multimode fiber at 850 nm and 980 nm, is protocol-independent (Ethernet and PCIe-based applications cited), and is offered as a straight cable plug, straight cable coupler, and angled PCB connector (same URL). Robustness is attributed in part to an Expanded-Beam Principle that enlarges the optically effective surface across the fiber transition to reduce dust/contaminant sensitivity and end-face wear (same URL).

Engineering implication: the announced combination of >50 Gbps over up to 40 m, IEEE 802.3cz compliance, and ISO 24581/ISO 8092/DIN 70214 alignment indicates a connector design intended to let automotive architects adopt optical links where copper reach or bandwidth becomes limiting, while the expanded-beam interface targets field robustness and mating durability. These are announced specifications and test claims, not independently verified results.

## Evidence gaps

Only one publisher-dated record was supplied, covering a single company; no other monitored interconnect companies have dated technical records in this set, so no activity is reported for them. The record is a company announcement: the >50 Gbps, 40 m, compliance, and dust/water test claims are not corroborated by independent test data or standards-body listings. No production-release, qualification-completion, or volume-deployment evidence is provided, and no interoperability results beyond the stated IEEE 802.3cz compliance are given. The announcement date (2026-10-01) should be confirmed against the publisher's page before citing.

## Technical developments

- BizLink announced an ecosystem partnership with ams OSRAM to co-develop optical interconnect solutions for AI scale-up domains, proposing a "wide-and-slow" architecture that distributes data across many parallel lower-speed channels instead of a few high-speed channels, targeting extended reach and ultra-low latency while preserving cost and power efficiency. The companies plan to demonstrate a connectorized multi-core fiber solution at ECOC 2026 (Spain, September 21–23), pairing a 2D addressable microVCSEL array at 850 nm with BizLink's fiber-to-fiber connector and optical packaging. Engineering implication: the parallel-channel approach shifts design emphasis toward connector alignment, multi-core fiber coupling, and array-level optical packaging rather than per-lane speed; the planned demonstrator is the relevant technical milestone to watch. Source: https://www.bizlinktech.com/zh-cn/news/bizlink-partners-with-ams-osram-to-advance-photonics-for-ai-data-center-interconnects

## Evidence gaps

- The BizLink/ams OSRAM item is a company press release describing a planned demonstrator; no measured link performance, power, latency, or reliability data are provided, so the architecture's claimed benefits remain unverified. Source: https://www.bizlinktech.com/zh-cn/news/bizlink-partners-with-ams-osram-to-advance-photonics-for-ai-data-center-interconnects
- No other monitored interconnect companies have publisher-dated technical records in this set, so no further engineering activity can be reported without inventing it.
